text:
maria: Opened PR to update the model catalog entry for Nebula3b embeddings — found an edge case where embeddings get effectively truncated when input tokens > 512 and we use the naive page+avg approach. Added a short migration note and an SDK example to do streaming/paging safely. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4820 - need quick review (docs + ML compatibility)

jon: Thanks — quick Q: did you run the embed sharding bench? The numbers in the PR look different from what we publish in the catalog throughput table.

maria: I ran a small local bench (attached csv) — paging adds ~20-30% CPU for the client side but network/TPS is similar. I wrote a recommendation to prefer shard_size=256 for long inputs; left a note to link to the canonical bench artifact instead of pasting raw numbers.

leo: Pinging eng-ml for compatibility wording on quantized variants. @ash can you confirm whether quantized Nebula3b behaves the same under paging? We should avoid giving blanket guarantees.

ash: Quick check: int8 quantized variant preserves embedding dimensionality, but we observe higher variance in L2 norms when we split tokens across pages and avg — especially with long-span tokens where attention context matters. Short summary to add to PR: "Quantized variants may show increased embedding variance when using disjoint paging; consider overlap=32 tokens or use model-backed streaming embedding when exact continuity of attention is required."

kate: Docs request: can we add a minimal python SDK v3 example that shows sharding + overlap? The pseudo-code in the PR is fine but we need copy-pasteable snippet for the model card. Also add a short note in the migration guide for customers moving from naive split-and-average.

maria: Done — added a python example in the PR. Code block below (also in the model card):

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")

def paged_embeddings(text, model="nebula3b-embed", shard_size=256, overlap=32):
    tokens = tokenize(text)
    embeddings = []
    for i in range(0, len(tokens), shard_size - overlap):
        shard = detokenize(tokens[i:i+shard_size])
        resp = client.embeddings.create(model=model, input=shard)
        embeddings.append(resp.embedding)
    # stitch with simple weighted-average (example only)
    return stitch_embeddings(embeddings, overlap)
```

jon: small nit — in SDK v3 the param was renamed to `chunk_size` in the last client release (we introduced aliasing earlier but prefer the new name). Can you use `chunk_size` in the snippet to match the published SDK?

maria: Good catch, updated snippet to `chunk_size`. Also added a one-line remark about fallback to the hosted variant if customers hit mismatch with on-prem quantized runtime.

docs-bot: deploy-preview available: https://deploy-preview.docs.redwood.ai/4820 (preview build succeeded) :white_check_mark:

leo: LGTM from docs side. Two asks before merge: 1) replace the inline bench numbers with a link to the benchmark artifact (so we don't have to update docs on every run) and 2) add a short test case in the docs repo that runs the example against a tiny fixture to avoid regressions.

jon: Agree with leo. I removed the table and pushed a commit linking to the bench artifact S3 URL. I can add a tiny CI step that runs the snippet in smoke mode.

maria: Done — removed numbers, added bench link and a docs-smoke test that runs the paged example against a 600-token fixture.

ash: I reviewed the wording for quantized caveat and it's accurate. Approving from ML/compatibility POV.

kate: Approved from docs, tests pass on the preview. :shipit:

maria: Thanks all — merging once the CI run finishes. Will follow up with an internal note to Support about the overlap recommendation so they can triage customer reports.

jon: Nice work. If we see more reports we should consider adding a small dedicated example page titled "Embedding continuity for long inputs" to the model catalog.

maria: Filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/1179 — will follow up post-merge.
